The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - XMLSpaceTest.testPreserveDOM() calls doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, " foo ").
  - doTest creates a JXPathContext over an XML document (XmlSpace.xml) using the DOM model and asserts that context.getValue("test/text[@id='preserve']") equals " foo ".
  - The test expects that leading and trailing spaces are preserved for the node with id="preserve" (this corresponds to xml:space="preserve" semantics in the XML).

- How the value is produced in the DOM model:
  - In the DOM model, node values are returned by org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.getValue(), which delegates to stringValue(node).
  - DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node):
    - For TEXT_NODE and CDATA_SECTION_NODE it does: return text == null ? "" : text.trim().
    - For COMMENT_NODE and PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE it also trims.
    - For element nodes, it concatenates child node values (without trimming each text child), but finally returns buf.toString().trim().

- Why this causes the failure:
  - Because stringValue unconditionally trims both individual text nodes (for TEXT/CDATA) and the final aggregated string (for elements), any leading or trailing whitespace in the element’s text content is removed.
  - The XML for this test case uses xml:space="preserve" (as implied by the test id "preserve"), so leading/trailing spaces should be preserved. However, DOMNodePointer.stringValue ignores xml:space and always trims.
  - Therefore, context.getValue("test/text[@id='preserve']") returns "foo" instead of " foo ", causing the assertion to fail.

- Alignment with the current bug report:
  - The user-reported issue states that JXPath automatically trims string values, e.g., <value> 1234 56</value> becomes "1234 56" when " 1234 56" is expected. This exactly matches the behavior in DOMNodePointer.stringValue due to unconditional trimming.
  - The failing test is specifically checking that trimming does not happen when xml:space="preserve", which the current implementation does not honor.

- Root cause:
  - org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node) unconditionally trims whitespace for DOM nodes and does not consider xml:space inheritance (preserve vs default). This leads to loss of leading/trailing spaces in text content and breaks xml:space="preserve" behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
